sections.heading: C2 — Licensing and occupant protection
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Licensing and occupant protection

FACT_ID: sec01-R01 | anchor: A02
A provisional license normally bars public-highway driving from midnight until five in the morning. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R02 | anchor: A02
The provisional nighttime restriction does not apply when a licensed driver aged twenty-one or older accompanies the driver. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R03 | anchor: A02
Family necessity is a permitted reason for provisional nighttime driving when supported by a parent’s or guardian’s signed statement. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R04 | anchor: A02
Medical necessity permits provisional nighttime driving when a parent or guardian provides a signed statement. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R05 | anchor: A02
Driving to or from work is a provisional nighttime exception when the driver’s employer provides a signed statement. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R06 | anchor: A02
Travel to or from school or a religious activity is a provisional nighttime exception with a signed statement from a school official, religious official, parent or guardian. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R07 | anchor: A02
A medical emergency is another exception to the provisional nighttime driving restriction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R08 | anchor: A02
The handbook describes driver licenses as having either four-year or eight-year validity. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R09 | anchor: A02
The renewal window described in the handbook begins ninety days before expiration and ends thirty days afterward. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R10 | anchor: A02
For renewal, the handbook directs a driver to bring the existing license and another identity document. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R11 | anchor: A02
Renewal can require vision or knowledge testing and, in special cases, a driving examination. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R12 | anchor: A02
A conviction for driving while impaired by alcohol or drugs can result in loss of driving privileges. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R13 | anchor: A02
Refusing an alcohol or drug test requested by a police officer can cost a driver the privilege to drive. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R14 | anchor: A02
Leaving a crash in which you are involved without identifying yourself can result in loss of driving privileges. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R15 | anchor: A02
False information on a driver-license application can lead to loss of driving privileges. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R16 | anchor: A02
Failing to settle a judgment against you for motor-vehicle-crash damages can put your driving privileges at risk. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R17 | anchor: A02
Attempting to alter your license information or using another person’s license when trying to buy alcohol can lead to loss of driving privileges. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R18 | anchor: A02
Failing to attend a reexamination requested by MVD can jeopardize the driver license. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R19 | anchor: A03
Using a vehicle for a felony or causing a death in a vehicle crash can result in loss of driving privileges. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R20 | anchor: A03
Accumulating excessive driving-record points can lead to loss of driving privileges. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R21 | anchor: A03
Allowing another person to use your driver license can lead to loss of driving privileges. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R22 | anchor: A03
Before driving, buckle your belt and check that every passenger uses a belt or a child restraint. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R23 | anchor: A03
The handbook directs drivers to lock the vehicle doors before setting off. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R24 | anchor: A03
Using a safety belt reduces the chance of death or injury in a crash. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R25 | anchor: A03
The handbook states that driving without a safety belt violates New Mexico law. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R26 | anchor: A03
A two-part belt system provides its intended protection when both its lap portion and its shoulder portion are worn. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R27 | anchor: A03
An automatic shoulder belt still requires fastening the separate lap belt. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R28 | anchor: A03
The staged handbook says children younger than twelve must use appropriate restraints whenever the vehicle moves. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R29 | anchor: A03
The staged handbook says a child younger than twenty-four months or lighter than sixty pounds must use an approved safety device. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R30 | anchor: A03
The handbook recommends securing children in the rear seat. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R31 | anchor: A03
The handbook directs caregivers never to secure a child in the front passenger seat, especially when that position has an air bag. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R32 | anchor: A03
Organizations may lend a child safety device to a caregiver who cannot afford one. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R33 | anchor: A03
The handbook gives the Traffic Safety Bureau information numbers as 505-827-0427 and 1-800-541-7952. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0006]
